# A rational minimal-circuit obstruction to projective cap-bias contraction

The simultaneous projective section-area minimum in
`candidate 85d2c2a949b59b29` is valid. The following proposed
closing comparison is false, even for a tetrahedron and a minimal positive
circuit of centroidal sections:

    |Σθ_i p_i−1/2| ≤ |Σθ_i p_i(projective)−1/2|.       (X)

Here the same central halfspaces and probability weights are retained,
and the projective image is the unique one with centroid0.

## 1. The simplex, point and stationary sections

Use the standard tetrahedron with barycentric coordinates ξ_0,...,ξ_3.
Let the common section centroid have barycentrics

    λ=(191/846, 518/2115, 527/2538, 2041/6345).

All four coordinates are positive, less than1/3, and sum to1. Translate
this point to0. The first cap has raw signed vertex values

    t=(14,11,−22,−4).

For a tetrahedral two-versus-two cap with values(p,q,−r,−s), its section
has successive barycentric vertices

    A=(r/(p+r),0,p/(p+r),0),
    B=(s/(p+s),0,0,p/(p+s)),
    C=(0,s/(q+s),0,q/(q+s)),
    D=(0,r/(q+r),q/(q+r),0).

Set α=ps/((p+r)(p+s)(q+s)), δ=qr/((p+r)(q+s)(q+r)).
The two triangles ABC and ACD have area ratio α:δ, as their cross
products are respectively−α n and−δ n for n=(q−p,−r−p,−s−p).
Thus their combined centroid is

    (A+C+[αB+δD]/(α+δ))/3.

Substitution of(14,11,22,4) gives exactly λ. The cap volume fraction is
p(α+δ)+q²/((q+s)(q+r)), by triangulating its three pyramids from vertex0.
The section coarea factor divided by tetrahedron volume is3(α+δ).
Here these values are626/1215 and47/810.

For vertex i, the central section with centroid λ has raw signed values
3 at i and3−1/λ_j at j≠i. Its edge intercepts are3λ_j, so its cap
fraction and normalized coarea factor are both
27Π_{j≠i}λ_j. These formulas prove that all four cuts below are proper
and have exactly the same section centroid.

Use the cuts:

    1. the displayed two-versus-two cap;
    2. the vertex3 cap;
    3. the complement of the vertex0 cap;
    4. the complement of the vertex1 cap.

## 2. Positive balance and minimality

Let q_i be section area times inward unit normal, divided by body
volume. Equivalently multiply each raw normal by its normalized coarea
factor. In coordinates(ξ_1,ξ_2,ξ_3), these vectors are

    q_1=(−47/270, −94/45, −47/45),
    q_2=(4743/44180, −11914/99405, 136493/99405),
    q_3=(1075607/596430, 1057238/497025, 136493/99405),
    q_4=(−1075607/596430, 46943/298215, −641359/1192860).

Give them probabilities with common denominator N=646372709662:

    θ=(220438125401,35599660824,204746742725,185588180712)/N.

Direct rational substitution gives Σθ_i=1 and Σθ_i q_i=0. All weights
are positive. Moreover

    det(q_1,q_2,q_3)=−1007454833/210241575≠0.

Thus the four vectors have rank3, their dependence space is
one-dimensional, and its unique positive dependence uses all four.
They form a minimal positive circuit.

Their cap fractions before the projective transformation are

    (626/1215,
     26070163/84096630,
     352142512/630724725,
     299138843/504579780).

The weighted mean is

    P=1570274946076/2908677193479.

## 3. The exact centroid-zero projective image

For any simplex with origin barycentrics λ, the centroid-zero
projective map has denominator at vertex i equal to1/(4λ_i).
Indeed the transformed vertex vectors are4λ_i(v_i−y), whose sum is0.
Those positive denominators arise from a unique affine denominator
1+ℓ·x because their λ-weighted mean is1. The image is therefore in
the admissible projective domain. The strictly convex volume argument
in the invariant note proves it is the unique projective volume minimum.

A central raw plane with original signed vertex values t_i acquires
signed values4λ_i t_i at the transformed vertices. Cap fractions are
computed in simplex barycentric coordinates by the formulas in §1;
for a one-versus-three cap the formula is a³/Π_j(a+b_j), where a is
its positive vertex value and−b_j are its negative values. Reversing
a cut complements its fraction. Applying these formulas gives

    (7600699714514571/14642033640793712,
     1308023834/3094640563,
     668014703/1190605028,
     2063099/3673043).

The weighted mean with the SAME θ is

    P'=3158781764622875088029132138218662810582905066533
       /5857054776644612955546677390460838594107476184416.

Exact subtraction gives

    P−P'=
      28806586307638718783098471763459517260148517939
      /52713492989801516599920096514147547346967285659744 >0.

Both means exceed1/2. In fact P>2699/5000 and
1/2<P'<2697/5000. Hence|P−1/2|>|P'−1/2|, contradicting(X).
Numerically P≈0.5398587886 and P'≈0.5393123140; the rational identities
above, not these decimals, certify the strict inequality.

Reversing all four cuts preserves their centroids, positive weights
and minimal balance. It gives means1−P≈0.4601412114 and
1−P'≈0.4606876860, both below1/2. Thus restricting a proposed
same-weight monotonic comparison to original mean below1/2 also does
not repair it.

Both original and transformed means remain above γ_3=27/64 after
this reversal. This example is not a counterexample to the weighted
stationary-section inequality or to the mixed-integer conjecture.
